job.title: Principal Advisor - Regulatory Strategy Implementation
job.description:
Are you an experienced professional regulator ready to deliver our regulatory practice reforms?

RSHQ is seeking a Principal Advisor – Regulatory Strategy Implementation professional who has the regulator expertise to work within the newly established Regulatory Strategy Implementation team. Reporting to the Director, this role will support the implementation of regulatory practice reforms and initiatives that deliver on RSHQ’s Regulatory Strategy and Regulatory Model Review recommendations.  

What you will do:

  • Plan, implement and maintain frameworks, policies, tools, systems, and processes to ensure delivery of improvements to RSHQ’s regulatory functions.
  • Provide expert advice and support to the agency on regulatory practice and reform matters.
  • Support decision-making of our operational teams and the frameworks in which they operate, while providing high quality guidance and training.
  • Contribute to the provisions of expert analysis and advice, including the preparation of concise correspondence, briefings, submissions and policy responses.
  • Help set RSHQ’s standards of regulatory practice, identifying and driving improvement in consistent, transparent and robust regulatory practice.  


What you will need to bring:

  • Demonstrated experience in regulatory agencies and/or operationalising regulatory frameworks.  
  • Proven ability to influence and direct the agency towards regulatory reform, with exceptional communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Established skill in risk-based problem identification and intervention planning.


The role description will outline any qualifications, licences and specific requirements of the role. If you are interested in this job, we encourage you to read the attached role description and talk to the contact officer.

  • Applications will remain current for a period of up to 12 months and may be considered for other vacancies (identical or similar).
  • Appointments are subject to criminal history checks in accordance with section 52 of the Public Sector Act 2022.
  • Prior to appointment, current and previous public sector employees are required to disclose any history of serious disciplinary action in accordance with section 71 of the Public Sector Act 2022.
  • All employees are required to disclose any interest/s that conflict, may conflict or may be perceived to conflict with the discharge of their duties in accordance with section 89, 182 or 183 of the Public Sector Act 2022.


For a confidential discussion please contact Ian Quinn at Dean & Ling Executive on 0403 343 097.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button or visit www.deanling.com.au

Applications close midnight 22 November 2026.

job.title: Coordinator Financial Accounting and Business Partnering
job.description:
At Central Highlands Regional Council, you'll have the opportunity to make a genuine and lasting impact on the communities, infrastructure and services that support one of Queensland's most diverse and significant regions.

Central Highlands Regional Council spans approximately 60,000 square kilometres, from Arcadia Valley in the south to the Peak Ranges in the north, and from Boolburra in the east to Bogantungan in the west. Managing more than $1.9 billion in community assets, Council delivers a diverse range of services through libraries, aquatic centres, customer service centres, 4,632 kilometres of roads, extensive parks and recreational facilities and a regional airport.

Central Highlands Regional Council is well positioned financially, with low debt levels, healthy cash balances, mature financial governance frameworks, and a long-term financial strategy already in place. This provides a strong platform for the successful candidate to contribute to the ongoing financial sustainability of the organisation and support Council's strategic priorities. We are seeking an accomplished finance professional to join Council as the second-in-command to the Manager Finance.      The Coordinator Financial Accounting and Business Partnering is a key Finance leadership position combining financial control, governance, business partnering and team leadership, while providing strategic support across the organisation. You will play a pivotal role in shaping financial performance, driving continuous improvement and contributing to the long-term sustainability of Council's operations and services.

Your work will include:

  • Providing leadership and strategic direction across Council's financial accounting, reporting and business partnering functions.
  • Partnering with the Manager Finance to shape financial strategy, organisational performance and long-term financial sustainability.
  • Leading the preparation and presentation of budgets and long term forecasts and reporting on financial performance outcomes to senior executives, Council and Audit and Risk Committee.
  • Manage the preparation of the statutory financial statements and coordination of external audit.
  • Influencing organisational decision-making through the provision of insightful financial analysis, commercial advice and risk-based recommendations.
  • Driving a culture of financial accountability, enabling leaders across the organisation to make informed and financially sustainable decisions.
  • Championing continuous improvement, systems optimisation and modern financial practices that enhance operational effectiveness and service delivery.
  • Developing and mentoring finance professionals while building leadership capability, succession readiness and team performance.
  • Acting as the Finance 2IC, providing leadership of the function and representing Council on financial matters in the absence of the Manager Finance.

Bring executive-calibre finance leadership

You understand that effective finance leadership extends beyond technical excellence. It requires the ability to influence decision-making, strengthen governance, manage risk and build capability across an organisation.

You are a trusted advisor who can translate complex financial information into meaningful strategic insights for executives and stakeholders. Equally comfortable in the boardroom and with operational leaders, you bring the judgement, credibility and commercial acumen to guide sound financial outcomes and support organisational performance.

You will bring significant experience in financial management, statutory reporting, budgeting, forecasting, internal controls and financial governance within a complex organisation. Your ability to lead people, challenge thinking constructively and drive continuous improvement will be highly valued.

While local government experience is advantageous, we welcome applications from accomplished finance professionals from the public or private sectors who have operated in senior finance leadership, Financial Controller, Finance Manager or equivalent roles.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Ian Quinn at Dean & Ling Executive on 0403 343 097.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button or visit www.deanling.com.au

Application will close at midnight on the 20 November 2026

For further information on Central Highlands Regional Council, please visit www.chrc.qld.gov.au

job.title: Executive Manager - Memberships, Partnerships & Growth
job.description:
An opportunity exists for an accomplished executive to lead membership experience, partnerships and commercial growth within an established membership organisation.

Combining strategic influence with direct accountability for results, this role will suit an experienced executive who has improved customer service while growing revenue. You will bring strong sales credentials, sound commercial judgement and the ability to empower managers to deliver.

Working closely with the CEO and the Executive leadership team, you will strengthen member value and translate business priorities into clear plans, agreed service standards and measurable outcomes.

A critical priority will be building strong alignment between Head Office and regional teams. You will ensure regional feedback and insights inform business decisions, while working cohesively with the General Managers who hold specialist expertise and key decision-making responsibilities.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Leading and developing managers, with clear expectations, appropriate authority and accountability for performance.
  • Driving membership acquisition and retention, alongside sponsorship, partnership and profitable events revenue.
  • Reviewing and improving the end-to-end member journey, using customer feedback, commercial insights and CRM data to identify priorities.
  • Developing agreed customer service standards alongside measures of member experience.
  • Improving CRM adoption and the use of information to support sales activity, service delivery and informed decisions.
  • Building effective relationships across the business to deliver consistent service and coordinated commercial outcomes.

You will bring demonstrated executive leadership experience and a record of delivering both commercial growth and service improvement. You will have successfully led managers and teams, exercised executive judgement and taken responsibility for business outcomes.

Your experience will include:

  • Direct sales leadership and personal accountability for revenue growth, supported by measurable results.
  • Commercial management, including budgets, profitability and performance targets.
  • Improving customer or member acquisition, retention and experience.
  • Developing partnerships, sponsorships or events that generate commercial value.
  • Leading change and strengthening collaboration across functions or locations.
  • Using data, customer insights and market intelligence to make decisions and hold teams accountable.

You will be a confident, collaborative leader who establishes trust with executive colleagues, welcomes specialist expertise and gives managers the support and authority to perform.

Relevant experience may come from membership organisations, hospitality, travel, tourism, sport, events or other businesses with strong customer relationships and commercial disciplines. Industry experience is useful, but your executive leadership capability, sales experience and evidence of results will be central to your success.

Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your executive leadership experience and achievements in sales, revenue growth and customer or member experience.

For a confidential discussion contact Mark Phillips, Managing Director, Dean & Ling Executive, on 0414 609 604 or mphillips@deanling.com.au.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button or visit www.deanling.com.au

Assessment will explore your executive leadership record, direct sales achievements, use of insights and ability to build effective relationships across a business.

job.title: Asset Accountant
job.description:
A career with purpose. A region with opportunity.

At Central Highlands Regional Council, you'll have the opportunity to make a genuine and lasting impact on the communities, infrastructure and services that support one of Queensland's most diverse and significant regions.

Central Highlands Regional Council spans approximately 60,000 square kilometres, from Arcadia Valley in the south to the Peak Ranges in the north, and from Boolburra in the east to Bogantungan in the west. Managing more than $1.9 billion in community assets, Council delivers a diverse range of services through libraries, aquatic centres, customer service centres, 4,632 kilometres of roads, extensive parks and recreational facilities and a regional airport.

Proud of its financial stability and with renewed energy across its leadership team, Council is focused on strengthening capability, improving systems and delivering sustainable outcomes for its communities.

More than numbers. More than an asset register.

Behind every community asset is a financial story. What it costs, how its value changes, when it needs to be renewed and how Council plans for its future.

As Asset Accountant, you'll play an important role in ensuring Council has accurate, reliable financial information to manage its infrastructure portfolio and make informed investment decisions.

Reporting to the Manager Finance, you'll work closely with finance, engineering, strategic asset management and program management, bringing together accounting expertise, asset information and practical business insights.

Your work will include:

  • Maintaining accurate fixed asset registers, asset accounting policies, procedures and financial controls.
  • Supporting annual asset revaluations, depreciation and disposals in accordance with accounting standards.
  • Maintenance of the Works in Progress (WIP) register and accurate recording of asset capitalisations.
  • Preparing asset accounting information for annual financial statements, external audit and long-term financial planning.
  • Assisting with financial analysis to support lifecycle costing, renewal forecasting and infrastructure investment planning.
  • Improving asset data integrity, reporting and processes across financial and asset management systems, including Asset MyData, TechnologyOne CiA and collaboration with GIS colleagues.
  • Manage the preparation and reconciliation of Property, Plant and Equipment (PP&E) disclosures for annual statutory financial statements.
  • Calculate and maintain contract asset and liability balances for externally grant funded projects in accordance with accounting standards and funding agreement requirements.
  • Working across Council to strengthen asset accounting practices, share knowledge and support continuous improvement.

You'll also have opportunities to contribute to broader financial accounting and planning activities as your experience develops.

Bring your accounting expertise. Build on it.

You may already be an experienced asset accountant looking for a new challenge, or a strong accountant keen to diversify your experience and develop a valuable specialisation.

We're interested in both.

You'll bring sound accounting knowledge, analytical skills, an understanding of financial reporting and a practical approach to systems, data and problem-solving. You'll be comfortable working with different stakeholders and interested in understanding how financial information supports infrastructure decisions.

Experience in asset accounting, infrastructure or local government will be highly regarded, but Council is equally interested in capable accountants with the ambition to learn and develop.

Specialist technical  support will be provided, creating an opportunity to build knowledge and progressively take ownership of the asset accounting function.

Already here? Or ready for a change of scenery?

For those already living in Emerald or the Central Highlands, this is an opportunity to progress your accounting career while contributing to the region you call home.

For those considering a move, Emerald offers the opportunity to build a rewarding professional career while enjoying the space, community connection and lifestyle of regional Queensland.

A thriving regional centre with schools, health services, sporting clubs, local businesses and a welcoming community, Emerald offers plenty for individuals and families alike.

Beyond work, Emerald offers plenty to explore, from the Sapphire Gemfields and Lake Maraboon to local events, sporting clubs and a strong sense of community.

With a diverse regional economy, established community facilities and air connections to Brisbane, Emerald offers a genuine opportunity to put down roots, raise a family or embrace a new chapter.

 Interested in finding out more?

Whether you're an experienced asset accountant or an ambitious accounting professional ready to develop in a new direction, we'd be pleased to have a conversation.  Reach out to Janine Jackson on    0409 802 806 or jjackson@deanling.com.au.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button or visit www.deanling.com.au

Applications close midnight 20 November 2026.

For further information on Central Highlands Regional Council, please visit www.chrc.qld.gov.au

job.title: Geotechnical Engineer
job.description:
As a seasoned and specialised Senior Consultant, I collaborate with a wide array of D’n’C Civil Contractors, Engineering Consultancies, and public sector employers who are actively seeking talented Geotechnical Engineers and Engineering Geologist. Operating out of Brisbane, I service clients across Australia, connecting skilled professionals with opportunities that align with their expertise and career aspirations.

Given the unprecedented levels of activity in infrastructure, disaster relief, and Olympics-related projects, my clients are urgently seeking experienced and competent engineers at all levels. Whether you're looking to work with small, agile firms or large, established organizations in the private or public sector, I have roles that can match your ambitions. My clients prioritize their staff's well-being, ensuring projects are delivered to high standards and completed safely.

Currently, we are seeking Civil Engineers and Geotechnical Engineers at all levels. Depending on your experience and the specific needs of the client, your responsibilities could include:

  • Conducting Site Investigations and Analysis
  • Engaging in Design and Engineering tasks
  • Providing Project Management Support
  • Collaborating with Clients and Stakeholders
  • Ensuring Health, Safety, and Environmental Compliance
  • Team and Business Leadership

To be considered, you ideally possess the following qualifications and attributes:

  • A tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering and/or Geotechnical Engineering,
  • Local experience in Australia or New Zealand—though international candidates are also welcome to apply
  • Experience with and of the following:
    • site investigations, producing both factual and interpretive reports, and using industry-standard design software (e.g., PLAXIS, WALLAP, Slope/W)
    • Familiarity with DTMR/RMS/VicRoads specifications, including main road and technical standards
    • Design & estimating – piling, ground improvement or bulk earthworks
    • Project delivery – piling or ground improvement
  • A collaborative spirit, thriving in multicultural team environments
  • Exemplary communication skills, both written and verbal
  • A genuine passion for engineering and a drive to excel in your field


My clients are offering full-time, permanent roles with significant career progression opportunities. Depending on your experience, you can expect:

  • A competitive base salary plus superannuation ($100k - $220k plus super)
  • Additional benefits such as mileage reimbursement or vehicle allowances, depending on the role
  • Genuine learning and development opportunities that can pave the way for career advancement
  • The chance to work with a dedicated team of engineering professionals who take pride in their work and ensure everyone gets home safely at the end of the day

If the above resonates with you and you want to take the grunt work out of your job search, get in touch today for a confidential discussion. Please contact Justin Bindman at 0431 821 593 or via email at jbindman@deanling.com.au.

job.title: Assistant Company Secretary
job.description:
This well-established superannuation trustee, part of a growing investment group, is known for its professional, supportive and collaborative culture and its commitment to delivering long-term value for members. As the organisation continues to strengthen its governance framework and processes, they are seeking an Assistant Company Secretary to provide practical, high-quality governance and secretariat support to the trustee Board and its Committees. This is a fully remote role, open to candidates based anywhere in Australia.

Reporting to the Company Secretary, you will coordinate the full lifecycle of Board and Committee meetings, from annual calendars, agendas and paper collation through to minutes, resolutions and action item tracking. You will support a range of Committees, including Risk, Audit and Compliance, Investment, Membership Services and Nominations and Remuneration. You will also work closely with Chairs, Directors and executives to improve the quality, clarity and timeliness of Board papers. You will support the Director and Responsible Person lifecycle, including appointments, inductions, declarations, conflicts and offboarding, and will maintain governance registers and records using Diligent and related systems. In addition, you will assist with ASIC and APRA obligations and support cyclical governance reviews, including fit and proper, skills and Board performance assessments. You will also contribute to governance uplift projects that make processes simpler and more reliable.

You will be an experienced governance professional, currently working as an Assistant Company Secretary, Governance Officer or Board Secretariat specialist. Superannuation experience is strongly preferred, and you will bring a sound working knowledge of trustee governance and the APRA-regulated environment. You will hold a tertiary qualification in law, business, commerce, governance or a related discipline, or have equivalent relevant experience, and will hold or be working towards the Graduate Diploma in Applied Corporate Governance from the Governance Institute of Australia. With highly developed written and verbal communication skills, you will have a proven track record in preparing Board and Committee materials and taking minutes. You will have a sound understanding of the Corporations Act as it relates to the company secretarial function. Highly organised and meticulous in your attention to detail, you will take pride in getting things right and will be confident following up Directors and executives to keep meetings and decisions on track. You will also bring an interest in continuing your professional development in superannuation and trustee governance.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: General Counsel
job.description:
A pioneering, founder-led business operating in the global energy sector, this rapidly growing organisation is developing technology and capability with the potential to reshape how energy is delivered at scale. Backed by a clear vision and strong momentum, the business is now entering a significant period of expansion, both in Australia and internationally. This General Counsel appointment offers the opportunity to lead and further develop the legal and governance function, strengthening its foundations and scaling it as the organisation grows.

Reporting directly to the Founder and as a key member of the leadership team, you will provide commercially pragmatic legal advice across energy contracts, general supply contracts, disputes, corporate, governance, and regulatory matters, acting as a key sounding board on strategy and risk. You will build on the existing legal frameworks, policies, processes, and systems, refining and strengthening them so they keep pace as operations expand into new markets. This is a genuinely broad, hands-on role, spanning strategic advice to the Founder and the advisory board through to day-to-day commercial and operational legal issues.

You are a trusted legal advisor with strong commercial judgement and a pragmatic, solutions-oriented approach to negotiation and risk. An admitted Australian legal practitioner with 10+ years’ experience across corporate, commercial, litigation, energy or in-house legal roles, you bring a broad skill set and the confidence to operate autonomously in a fast-moving, evolving environment. Whether you are currently leading a legal function or are a senior lawyer seeking the next step in your career, you will be ready to take ownership of the legal agenda and grow with the business. Exposure to litigation and dispute management will be well regarded, as will a demonstrated ability to build and scale legal systems and processes in a growing business. You are curious, keen to learn, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to move seamlessly between strategic thinking and hands-on execution. Experience in energy, infrastructure, technology, or other founder-led, high-growth or start-up environments, will be highly regarded.

job.title: Legal Counsel
job.description:
Our client is a well-respected market leader in a complex, highly regulated industry, known for its collaborative culture and commitment to its customers, partners and the communities it serves. Due to continued growth, they are now seeking a Legal Counsel to join their established in-house legal team. This is a great opportunity for a lawyer with strong contracting experience who is looking to step into a high-impact in-house environment or deepen their expertise within a large, multifaceted organisation.

As part of a close-knit and commercially focused Legal team, you will step into a broad and engaging role, providing end-to-end legal support across the business. In this varied position, you will review, advise on and negotiate a wide range of contracts and commercial agreements; maintain and update precedent documents and standard-form templates; assist in managing disputes and regulatory matters; advise on media responses and complaints handling; support the remediation and rectification of issues and incidents; and review correspondence with customers, providers and regulators.

You will be a confident, pragmatic and solutions-oriented lawyer with approximately 4–7 years' post-admission experience in contracting and commercial law gained in private practice or an in-house environment. Prior experience within a large, regulated services business including healthcare providers or health insurers will be highly regarded. Strong drafting skills, sound commercial judgment, the ability to communicate complex legal issues clearly and a genuine interest in understanding the business will be key to your success. This role will suit someone who thrives in a fast-paced, stakeholder-rich environment, is comfortable navigating regulatory complexity and brings a calm, constructive approach to sensitive matters.

If you're ready to join a supportive, high-performing legal team where your expertise will be genuinely valued and your career development actively supported, we would love to hear from you.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
job.description:
As a 3rd generation family run business, our client represents what can be achieved by a group of loyal dedicated professionals with a clear vision and robust work ethic. This organisation has been recognized internationally as an industry leader in design and fabrication of bulk liquid storage and transportation systems. They boast an impressive client base (domestic and international) and have an enviable pipeline for work for the foreseeable future.


The Senior Mechanical Engineer provides advanced mechanical engineering, design, analysis, and technical leadership services to the business. The role leads the development of compliant, safe, practical, and commercially effective engineering solutions, while mentoring junior engineers and contributing to the continuous improvement of engineering standards, systems, and processes.

  • Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering, recognised by Engineers Australia
  • Minimum 5 years' relevant mechanical engineering experience, ideally within fabrication/manufacturing and heavy vehicle environments
  • Strong mechanical design, engineering calculations and 3D modelling skills, with experience designing steel and aluminium fabricated structures
  • Demonstrated experience in FEA of weldments and assemblies
  • Experience with pneumatic and hydraulic system design
  • Competency with Autodesk Inventor/AutoCAD and related engineering software
  • Understanding of ISO 9001 and relevant engineering standards and processes
  • Preferred: Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) and bulk fuel tanker or trailer experience.

In addition to the above, you will need to be team oriented and a genuine down-to-earth professional as this is a team of loyal, long tenured staff who love to produce top quality work and keep their customer base satisfied. 

If you are successful in obtaining this position, you will receive a highly competitive salary package, composed of base salary and superannuation. You play an integral part in successful Australian business and benefit from the range of other benefits throughout the course of your employment.

If you are interested in applying for the role, please submit your current CV  via the Apply button or contact Justin at jbindman@deanling.com.au for more information about the role.
